facts.text: On this day in 1850, California became the 31st U.S. state — just 18 months after the gold rush began. It was admitted so fast it skipped the territorial phase entirely.
On this day in 1948, North Korea was formally established, making the Korean peninsula's division only 78 years old — younger than many of its living citizens.
More people live inside a circle drawn 4,000 km around Bangladesh than outside it. That single radius captures over half of all humanity.
Monaco has a higher density of millionaires than any nation on Earth — roughly one in three residents. It also has no income tax and fits inside Central Park.
The city of Chongqing, China, has more people than Australia, Canada, or Saudi Arabia. Most Westerners cannot place it on a map.
On this date in 1965, the U.S. government raised the federal debt ceiling to $328 billion. It has been raised over 100 times since.
On Sept 9, 1947, the Dow closed at 184. It would take another 25 years just to crack 1,000.
The NYSE was created in 1792 by 24 brokers signing a deal under a buttonwood tree. The tree is gone. The exchange handles $20 trillion in annual trades.
Saudi Aramco briefly surpassed $2 trillion in market cap in 2022 — making it worth more than the entire GDP of Italy, Canada, or South Korea.
The word 'salary' comes from the Latin 'salarium' — payment in salt. Roman soldiers were literally paid in a seasoning.
On this day in 1839, John Herschel made the first glass-plate photograph — capturing light on a surface so stable that some of his plates still exist, holding 187-year-old photons in silver.

On September 9, 1976, Mao Zedong died — and autopsies revealed his body produced so much formaldehyde naturally post-death that embalmers initially over-injected him, swelling his face beyond recognition.
A neutron star packs more mass than the Sun into a sphere the size of a city. A single teaspoon of its matter would weigh roughly a billion tons on Earth.
Your body replaces the lining of your small intestine every two to four days. The organ absorbing your lunch today is largely tissue that did not exist last week.

The universe is not merely expanding — the expansion is accelerating. Every galaxy beyond our local group is retreating faster each year, and most of the observable universe is already receding faster than light can ever reach us.
On this day in 1776, the Continental Congress officially named the new nation 'United States' — the iPhone is closer in time to that vote than the vote is to the invention of the printing press.
On this day in 1956, Elvis Presley appeared on Ed Sullivan, watched by 60 million Americans — roughly 82% of the entire television audience, a share no broadcast has touched since.
Oxford University was already 300 years old when the Aztec Empire was founded. Europe's oldest university makes the Aztecs look like a startup.
The fax machine was invented in 1843 — 33 years before the telephone. You could fax a document before you could call anyone to tell them it was coming.
Cleopatra lived closer in time to the Moon landing than to the construction of the Great Pyramid. Ancient Egypt's timeline dwarfs our intuitions about antiquity.
Sonder (n.): the sudden awareness that every passerby has a life as vivid and complex as your own. Coined by John Koenig in 2012, it spread so fast that many now assume it has ancient roots.
Hiraeth (n.): a Welsh word for a longing for a home that may never have existed — grief, nostalgia, and yearning fused into one untranslatable ache.
On this day in 1791, the District of Columbia was named — not for a person present, but for Columbus, who never set foot on North American soil. The capital of a nation bears a ghost's geography.

Mamihlapinatapai: a Yaghan word from Tierra del Fuego describing the shared, wordless look between two people who both want something but neither will initiate. Guinness once listed it as the most succinct word in existence.

On this day in 1776, the United States officially named itself — the Continental Congress replaced 'United Colonies' with 'United States.' The word 'states' was chosen deliberately to assert sovereignty, not just unity.

On this date in 2017, China's PBOC declared ICOs illegal and ordered all fundraising halted immediately — triggering a 40% Bitcoin drop within days and permanently reshaping how projects structured token sales to avoid securities classification.

On this date in 2015, Ethereum processed its first non-test transaction on mainnet, moving 31,000 ETH — a network then worth roughly $400,000 that would peak above $500 billion in market cap six years later.
Bitcoin's timelock opcode, OP_CHECKLOCKTIMEVERIFY, was only activated in 2015 — despite Satoshi encoding the raw nLockTime field into the very first version of the protocol in 2009.

The DAO hack of 2016 didn't exploit Solidity — it exploited a logical assumption. The attacker called the withdrawal function recursively before the balance updated, draining 3.6M ETH through a flaw in expected execution order.

Ethereum validators don't confirm which transactions they saw first — the protocol has no concept of mempool arrival time, making 'first come, first served' fairness architecturally impossible at base layer without external MEV mitigation.

On this date in 2016, Google DeepMind's AlphaGo paper was published in Nature — the first AI to defeat a professional Go player without handicap, using a tree search over two neural nets trained on 30 million human moves.

On this date in 2009, ImageNet launched publicly. The dataset that would trigger deep learning's dominance had 3.2 million images across 4,000 categories — assembled by paying Mechanical Turk workers fractions of a cent per label.
GPT-4's training run is estimated to have consumed roughly 50 gigawatt-hours of electricity — comparable to the annual consumption of 4,500 average US homes, for a single model training pass.

The transformer architecture, now the backbone of nearly every major language model, was proposed in 2017 by eight authors at Google. Six of the eight have since left to found or lead competing AI companies.

Chinchilla scaling laws (2022) showed most large language models were undertrained relative to their size — meaning billions in compute had been systematically misallocated across the entire field for years before the correction.
